key_insight: Shallow QAOA mixer design faces two complementary bottlenecks: probability transport across configurations and finite-depth causal reach across the problem graph.
engineering_relevance: Problem-aligned two-local mixers can improve solution quality at fixed QAOA depth, but greater causal reach alone does not guarantee better performance.
method: Derive first-order mixer-dependent objective bounds and connect them through a graph-Laplacian identity.
Bound achievable concentration using layer-wise ℓ1 spreading of the mixer unitary.
Evaluate X+XX and X+YY mixers with k-hop causal radius at most (k+1)p.
evidence_signal: Numerical studies on cycles, circular ladders, and high-girth regular bipartite graphs found both augmented mixers outperforming X at equal depth; X+YY at depth p came within about one approximation-ratio point of X at depth 2p in examined reach-matched cases.
watch_item: Results concern best-found numerical solutions on selected graph families; equal causal reach does not imply equal performance.
paper_title: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach
